FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Chemical Hazards Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. p -nitroaniline is used to considerable extent as an intermediate in the preparation of azo and azoic dyes and for the production of p-phenylene diamine, a rather important, intermediate and dye. p-nitroaniline gets readily absorbed through skin and is a powerful methemoglobin former. In the preparation of this code of safety, considerable assistance has been derived from the following publications: a) Encyclopaedia of chemical technology by Raymond K. Kirk and Donald F. Othmer. b) Dangerous properties of industrial materials -- N. Irving Sax seventh edition. c) Occupational health and safety -- International Labour Office, Geneva.

IS 13447 : 1992

Indian Standard p-NITROANILINE -- CODE OF SAFETY
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard describes properties of pnitroaniline, the nature of hazards associated with it and essential information on personal protective equipment, storage, handling, labelling, transportation, spillage and leakage and waste disposal; fire prevention and fire fighting training and health monitoring, and first aid. 1.2 This code, however, does not deal with the specifications for design of buildings, process equipment, plant lay-out, storage vessels, etc. The code also does not cover the specifications of the material. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards are necessary adjuncts to the standard: IS No. 4155 : 1966 4167 : 1966 Title Glossary of terms relating to chemical and radiation hazardous chemicals Glossary of terms relating to air pollution 4.2.2 It is best prepared by treating p-nitrochlorobenzene with excess ammonia under pressure. It may also be prepared by nitrating acetanilide to form p-nitroacetanilide ( m. p. 214-216�C ) and hydrolysing this with caustic or mineral acid. 4.2.3 4.2.4 4.2.5 4.2.6 Melting Point -- 148.5�C. Boiling Point -- 332.0�C. Relative Density -- 1.424. Vapour Pressure -- 1 mm at 142.4�C.

4.2.7 Solubility It is soluble in 1 250 parts of cold water, 45 parts of boiling water, 20 parts of alcohol and 22 parts of ether. It is also soluble in benzene, methanol and mineral acids. 4.3 Chemical Properties 4.3.1 On decomposition, it emits toxic nitrogen dioxide. 4.4 Fire and Explosion Hazard Properties 4.4.1 Fire and explosion hazard is slight when exposed to heat, flame or mechanical shock. 4.4.2 Flash Point ( Close Cup ) -- 199�C. 5 HEALTH EFFECTS INFORMATION 5.1 TLV LD50 oral -- rat LD50 oral -- muss LD50 oral -- guineapig 5.3 Health Effects Acute symptoms of exposure are flushing of face, headache, nausea, vomiting, weakness, increased pulse rate and respiratory rate, instalvity and convulsion. It may induce stupor, cynosis and methemoglobinemia. 5.3.1 In less acute exposure which has been prolonged over some weeks or months, there is usually hemoglobinemia, chronic exposure can cause liver damage. 1 AND TOXICITY

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this code, the definitions given in IS 4155 : 1966 and IS 4167 : 1966 shall apply. 4 GENERAL PROPERTIES 4.1 General Information 4.1.1 Common Names -- Fast Red GG Base. 4.1.2 Chemical Names -- p-nitroaniline, l-amino4-nitrobenzene. 4.1.3 Structural Formula -- 4.1.4 Molecular Formula -- C6H6N2O2. 4.1.5 Molecular Mass -- 138. 4.2 Physical Properties 4.2.1 Description, Colour and Physical State -- p-nitroaniline is a bright yellow crystalline material.

-- 3 mg/m3 -- 750 mg/kg -- 810 mg/kg -- 450 mg/kg

5.2 Routes of Entry -- Oral, respiratory and skin.

IS 13447 : 1992 5.3.2 In less acute exposure which has been prolonged over some weeks or months, there is usually hemolysis of the red blood cells followed by stimulation of the bone marrow and attempts at regeneration. The red cells may show stippling, immature cells may be present. The white blood cells usually show little change either in number morphology. The liver may be affected with production of jaundice. The urine is frequently dark brown or wine coloured. 8 SPILLAGE/LEAKAGE AND WASTE DISPOSAL 8.1 Spillage/Leakage 8.1.1 In case of spillage remove all ignition sources. 8.1.2 Scrap up with a nonsparkling scoop and place in a covered metal container for disposal. Those involved in clean up should use protective equipment. Dispose off the scrap by burning in a remote open pit or depositing in a sanitary landfill. 8.2 Waste Disposal Dispose off the collected waste material by incineration in a furnace, there should be arrangement for water washing of floors/area. 9 FIRE PREVENTION AND FIRE FIGHTING 9.1 Good house keeping and strict adherence to all standing orders will avert any mishap involving p-nitroaniline. 9.2 To fight fire use water spray or mist form/ dry chemical/carbon dioxide extinguishers. 10 TRAINING AND HEALTH MONITORING 10.1 Training Safety in handling p -nitroaniline depends to a great extent upon the effectiveness of employees education proper safety instructions, intelligent supervision and the use of safe equipments. 10.2 Health Monitoring Provide regular medical monitoring of those exposed to this material in the work place. It is based on blood and urine analysis. Routine periodic examinations for each workman should include history, medical observation, blood pressure, pulse, mass and blood and urine analysis. 11 FIRST AID 11.1 Skin Contact Wash area of contact with soap and water. irritation persists get medical attention. If

6 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT
Protective equipments should include protective clothing full face masks with filters for organic vapours and self contained breathing apparatus or masks with air line supply systems may be necessary. Personal protective equipment such as gloves, goggles, boots and suit should be used when handling and transporting p-nitroaniline. 7 STORAGE, HANDLING, LABELLING AND TRANSPORT 7.1 Storage a) Do not store close to those materials that pose fire or explosion hazard; b) All room where p-nitroaniline is stored should be essentially flameproof type only. All plant and machinery handling p-nitroaniline shall be effectively earthed for controlling of undesirable static electricity; and c) Bulk storage areas should be away from all sources of open flame, heaters, furnaces and welding or other flame or spark producing equipments. 'NO SMOKING' signs should be conspicuously displayed in the area. 7.2 Handling Care should be exercised while loading and unloading p-nitroaniline by employing carefully instructed and reliable personnel. 7.3 Labelling Label indicating 'Poison' should be displayed. 7.4 Transport This is classified as class 6.1, that is, Poisonous ( Hazard ) Substances. According to UN Classification, U. N. No. 1661 such label has to be displayed on containers and on vehicle while transporting on road. 7.4.1 For transport of p-nitroaniline drums of approved design and construction as per instructions laid down with polythene liners must be used. 2

11.2 Eye Contact Immediately wash with plenty of water including under the eye lids. If irritation persists, get medical attention.

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well denned system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
